Files saved by an older version are not encrypted: the app deletes them after 30 days, except the newest file and latest.json of each match, which stay readable until you delete that match's folder. Only your user account can open the folder.

home.q_createMatch: How do I create a new match?
home.a_createMatch: Signed in, tap “SV match”: pick today's home game of your club from the list, or enter the game yourself. Signed out, tap “New match”: a full match without an account. You can pick the game from the schedule and import the Einsatzliste, but saved teams, club lists and the referee directory need a sign-in; the match stays on this device, with a backup under its backup code. “Test match” and “Easy match” are below. An official match has rosters, officials and signatures. A test match is for practice. An easy match is unofficial: no rosters and no signatures. “Scoreboard” is no match at all: just the points and sets of two teams on the whole screen, for a friendly or a training game. It stays on this device. In the Global tool, “Match” starts a full match without signing in.
home.tip_createMatch: Start a new match here: SV match (signed in), New match (signed out), test or easy, or open a plain scoreboard.
home.q_officialVsTest: What is the difference between official and test matches?
home.a_officialVsTest: An official match needs both rosters (at least 6 players each), the officials and, before the first serve, the signatures. When you are signed in, it is saved on the server for the referee, the livescore and the backups. A test match has invented teams for practice. It is never saved on the server; referee and bench tablets can still follow it (“Switch to test matches” on the tablet).
home.q_continueMatch: How do I continue a match?
home.a_continueMatch: The app always opens on Home. The card at the top shows the match on this device: the teams, the score, when it was last saved and its state. Tap “Continue match” to go back in. A reload of the page goes straight back into the match.
home.tip_continueMatch: Tap here to go back into the match on this device.
home.q_deleteMatch: How do I delete a match?
home.a_deleteMatch: Tap “Delete match”, or “Delete” in the “On this device” list. An official match asks for the game PIN. This deletes the match on this device and on the server. A copy that is closed on the server or scored on another device is only removed from this device. The dialog warns you when the copy holds changes the server does not have.
home.tip_deleteMatch: Tap here to delete the current match.
home.q_restoreMatch: How do I restore a match from backup?
home.a_restoreMatch: Tap “Restore match”. Choose “Restore from cloud backup” (game number and game PIN, then “Search cloud backups”), a backup under “Saved on this device or a drive”, or “Restore from local file” (“Select backup file”). Check the “Restore preview”, then tap “Confirm restore”. In the Global tool, “Restore from the online backup” asks for the backup code, then the referee PIN.
home.tip_restoreMatch: Tap here to restore a match from a cloud or local backup.
home.q_settings: How do I change the language or settings?
home.a_settings: The language is in the menu (☰) of the header. The other settings are in “Options”: on Home, in Match setup, or on the scoring screen under Match › Options. There you find “Tool” (Swiss or Global, on Home), “Theme” (“Light”, “Dark” for a dim hall, “E-ink” in black and white for bright light), “Show tap hints” (the small finger on the buttons you can tap now) and “Set 2-3 interval duration” (the break between sets 2 and 3; when it is extended to 10 minutes, switch on “10-minute interval after set 2” in Match info instead).
home.q_backgroundHome: Why did the app go back to Home?
home.a_backgroundHome: After 15 minutes or more in the background (another app, the screen off), the app shows Home. Nothing is closed or deleted: tap “Continue match”. Time with the screen on, such as a long set break, does not count.
home.q_matchStates: What do the labels on a match mean?
home.a_matchStates: “Scoring here”: this device scores it. “On another device”: another device took the match over. “Closed on the server”: the match is approved or closed. “Not checked”: the app could not ask the server (offline, signed out or no answer). “Unsent changes”: some changes are not on the server yet. A closed or moved copy opens read-only.
home.a_cleanUp: When the same game is on this device more than once, Home tells you. “Clean up” removes only the extra copies that hold nothing of their own. It asks first, and nothing changes on the server.
home.a_tool: At the first open the app asks “How do you use OpenVolley?”. “Swiss”: Swiss league games with sign-in, the game list, the Einsatzliste, club rosters and the cloud. “Global”: any tournament or friendly, no sign-in, games and rosters from Excel; teams and players stay on this device. Change it later in “Options” › “Tool”, as long as no match is on this device.
home.q_dashboards: Can this phone or tablet be the referee or bench tablet?
home.a_dashboards: Yes. On a phone or tablet, the menu (☰) on Home has “Referee dashboard” and “Bench dashboard”. They open the referee or bench screen on this device; “Back to scorer” in its menu brings you back. Not on a computer and not during a match.
home.q_gamePin: What is the game PIN on Home?
home.a_gamePin: For an official match, Home shows its “Game PIN” under “Restore match”. Keep it: you need it to delete the match, to restore it and to continue it on another device.
home.q_login: What does signing in give me?
home.a_login: Tap “Login” on Home. With an account the app loads the Swiss league games (“Load match from schedule”), your saved teams, your club's licence lists (“Add from club”) and the referee directory, and your official matches are saved in the cloud while you score. Without an account, test, easy and new matches work too; they stay on this device.
home.q_support: Where do I get help or report a problem?
home.a_support: The “?” button opens the help of the screen you are on, with a short video and “Show me”. “Support & feedback” on Home has the help pages and a form for a question or a problem: leave “Include diagnostics” on, it adds what was done in the app in the last two hours and its errors (never passwords, PINs or typed text), so we can see what happened.
home.a_scoreboardTool: A simple scoreboard for any game, without a scoresheet: “Point for Home” and “Point for Away” add a point, “One point off” takes one back, “Swap sides”, “Next set” and “New game”. Nothing is saved as a match. To show a scored match on a TV, use Match › “Show on a scoreboard” on the scoring screen.
home.q_liveScreen: What is the live screen in Options?
home.a_liveScreen: “Start a live screen” shows the score of every court of your event on TVs or a beamer, for any match. Start it on one scorer device and type its “Live screen code” on the other scorer devices (“Join”). Only the score goes online (team names, points, sets). On a smart TV, open its web browser at the address shown.
home.q_effects: The app is slow on my tablet: what can I do?
home.a_effects: Options › “Effects and speed”: “Check this device” measures how fast it is (about a second, nothing leaves the device) and recommends lighter settings. You can also switch off “Blur behind dialogs” and “Animations”, turn off “Seconds on the clock”, and turn off “Sharp PDF” for a faster scoresheet preview. Home offers the check once; run it again any time from Options on Home.
home.q_maintenance: What do the buttons at the end of Options do?
home.a_maintenance: “Download backup now” saves a backup file of this device's matches. “Show activity log” lists what the app did, and “Export diagnostics (.jsonl)” saves it as a file for support. “Check for updates” looks for a new app version. “Clear cache” deletes cached files and reloads the app; your settings stay. “Clear all (includes settings)” also resets your settings: use it only when support asks you to.
home.q_tapHints: What is the small finger on the buttons?
home.a_tapHints: It marks the buttons you can tap right now (scoring screen, Match setup, coin toss). If you find it too busy, switch off “Show tap hints” in Options.

matchSetup.q_matchInfo: How do I fill in match information?
matchSetup.a_matchInfo: On the “Match info” card, tap “Create match” (later “Edit”). Enter the game number, date, time, city, hall and league, the match format, and both team names. All of them are needed. The referees' e-mail and each team's contact e-mail are optional. After the coin toss, Match › “Edit match info” changes the match details, the officials, the team contacts and each team's shirt colour; the team names stay as they are.
matchSetup.tip_matchInfo: This card holds the match information. Tap “Create match” or “Edit” to change it.
matchSetup.q_teamColors: How do I set the team names and colours?
matchSetup.a_teamColors: The team names are in the match info. On each team's card, tap the shirt next to “Select colour” to pick the shirt colour. The app warns you when the two colours are close.
matchSetup.tip_teamColors: Tap the shirt to pick this team's shirt colour.
matchSetup.q_addPlayers: How do I add players to a team roster?
matchSetup.a_addPlayers: Tap “Edit roster” on the team's card. In the “Add new player” row, enter the number (1-99), last name, first name and the licence number (“Licence/DoB”: for someone without a licence, the date of birth), then tap “Add”. The number can wait until later. A team needs at least 6 players, not counting the liberos, and at most 14.
matchSetup.tip_addPlayers: Enter a player here and tap “Add”. A team needs at least 6 players, not counting the liberos.
matchSetup.q_importPdf: How do I import a roster from PDF?
matchSetup.a_importPdf: In “Edit roster”, keep “Local” selected and tap “Upload PDF”. Choose the team's roster PDF or the Einsatzliste, then tap “Import PDF”. It replaces the players and the bench officials. With more than 14 players, tick who plays. Then check the dates of birth, enter missing shirt numbers, and set the captain and the liberos. A date of birth on 1 January is often a placeholder (01.01.1900 when the date is not known) or an import error: the roster lists these people above the players. Correct the dates you know. The coin toss does not ask about them.
matchSetup.tip_importPdf: Tap here to import the players from a roster PDF.
matchSetup.q_importPhoto: Can I import the Einsatzliste from a photo?
matchSetup.a_importPhoto: Yes. In “Edit roster”, keep “Local” selected and tap “Photo of the list”. Take a photo of the printed list or choose a picture of it (a screenshot works too; zoom in so the table fills it). Drag the four corners onto the page, then tap “Read the list”: the photo is read on this device, not sent and not kept. Check the rows: a red field must be fixed, an amber one checked. Shirt numbers, the captain (C, K or a circled number) and liberos (L) written on the list are taken for this game; numbers left blank come from the saved team. Nothing changes until you tap “Use”. A PDF of the list is read more reliably than a photo.
matchSetup.tip_importPhoto: Tap here to read the Einsatzliste from a photo.
matchSetup.a_liberos: In the roster, choose “Libero 1” or “Libero 2” in the libero column. A team has at most 2 liberos. With more than 12 players it needs 2.
matchSetup.tip_liberos: Choose “Libero 1” or “Libero 2” here to make this player a libero.
matchSetup.q_captain: How do I set the team captain?
matchSetup.a_captain: Tap “C” next to the player in the roster. Each team needs one captain.
matchSetup.tip_captain: Tap “C” to make this player the team captain.
matchSetup.q_benchOfficials: How do I add bench officials?
matchSetup.a_benchOfficials: In “Edit roster”, tap “+ Add bench official”. Enter the coach, the assistant coaches, the physiotherapist and the doctor. A coach is needed, and a team has at most 5 bench officials.
matchSetup.tip_benchOfficials: Add the coach and the other bench officials here.
matchSetup.q_proceed: How do I proceed to the coin toss?
matchSetup.a_proceed: When every card is complete, tap “Coin toss” at the bottom. If it is greyed out, the yellow “!” next to it shows what is missing, for example players without a shirt number: tap it (“Click to see what's missing”) for the list.
matchSetup.tip_proceed: Tap here to go to the coin toss. Every required field must be complete first.
matchSetup.q_loadSchedule: Can I load the game from the schedule?
matchSetup.a_loadSchedule: Yes. On the “Match info” card, tap “Load match from schedule”. Choose the gender and the league, then the game. The app fills in the game number, the teams, the date, the time, the hall and the referees. It needs an internet connection. Then set the team colours and the short names.
matchSetup.a_officials: The 1st referee and the scorer, with the scorer's date of birth. Signed in, the scorer is you. “Database” picks a referee from the list. The 2nd referee, the assistant scorer and the line judges are optional (switch them on). The 2nd referee and the assistant scorer sign at the match end when they are entered.
matchSetup.q_rosterUpload: Can the coach send the roster?
matchSetup.a_rosterUpload: Yes. In “Edit roster”, choose “Remote” and tap “Generate PIN”. Give the coach the game number and this upload PIN. The coach opens roster.openvolley.app, picks the game and the team, enters the PIN and uploads the roster PDF. “Roster uploaded” then appears (“Check server for rosters” checks for it, and the panel checks again on its own while it is open): tap “Preview”, then “Accept” or “Reject”.
matchSetup.q_pins: Where are the PINs for the tablets?
matchSetup.a_pins: The game PIN is on the match info page (“Create match” or “Edit”), where “Send PIN by email” can send it to you, and on Home. Keep it: you need it to delete or restore the match. The referee and bench PINs are in “Connect tablets”. During the match, Match › Show PINs shows them all.
matchSetup.a_backups: At the top of Match setup, tap “Backups”. “Cloud” is always on while you score signed in (a test match is never sent). “This device”: the desktop and Android apps keep a file of the match themselves; in Chrome or Edge, “Select backup folder” keeps one in a folder you pick; other browsers download a file at set end and match end. “Removable drive”: the desktop app copies every backup to each USB stick plugged in; in Chrome or Edge, choose a folder on the stick.
matchSetup.q_teamContact: Can the teams get the final scoresheet by e-mail?
matchSetup.a_teamContact: Yes. Each team can have a “Team contact email (optional)” on the match info page, and each referee an “Email (optional)”. Only the scorers of this match see these addresses. During the match, change them in Match › “Edit match info” › “Team contacts”.
matchSetup.q_afterCoinToss: Can I change the setup after the coin toss?
matchSetup.a_afterCoinToss: Once the coin toss is confirmed, Match setup is read-only, except the shirt colours: tap a team's shirt to change it. In the scoring screen, Match › “Edit match info” changes the hall, the game number, the date, the officials, the team contacts and each team's short name and shirt colour, and “Edit home roster” or “Edit away roster” a roster. Everything else goes through Match › “Corrections”.
matchSetup.q_sentRoster: A team sent its roster ahead: what do I do?
matchSetup.a_sentRoster: Its card shows “Roster sent by …”. Tap “Show” to look at it, then “Accept” to load it, and check it with the coach (“Not now” leaves it for later). If the coach and the captain signed ahead, their signatures come with it.
matchSetup.q_clubPlayers: What do the green and gray shields mean?
matchSetup.a_clubPlayers: For a team of your club, each roster and bench row shows a shield (in landscape). Green: the person is in the club's licence lists; a dot means the club knows a first name or date of birth the row lacks: tap to fill it in. Gray: typed by hand: tap to link the row to someone in the club's lists. “Add from club” adds players from the lists.
matchSetup.q_rosterSignatures: Can the coach and the captain sign in Match setup?
matchSetup.a_rosterSignatures: Yes, if you like: “Edit roster” › “Signatures”. If that team's players or bench change after signing, its signatures are removed and they sign again.
matchSetup.q_back: How do I get back to Home from Match setup?
matchSetup.a_back: Tap “← Back” at the top, next to “Scoresheet” and “Options”. The match stays on Home: “Continue match” opens it again.
matchSetup.q_gamePinNotice: What is the game PIN dialog after “Create match”?
matchSetup.a_gamePinNotice: For a new official match the app shows its game PIN. Write it down: you need it to restore the match, to continue it on another device and to reopen it. “Send to my email” mails it to your account's confirmed address; for another address, type it and tap “Open in mail app” (nothing goes through the server then).
matchSetup.q_scorerLicence: Why can't I create the match?
matchSetup.a_scorerLicence: The scorer's licence number is needed (for someone without a licence, the date of birth). Until it is filled in, “Create match” stays greyed and the warning beside it says so, with anything else that is missing (“Click to see what's missing”).
matchSetup.q_showRosters: Where do I see both rosters at once?
matchSetup.a_showRosters: “Show rosters” under the team cards lists both rosters with numbers, licences, liberos, captain and bench officials; “Hide rosters” closes them. During the match: Match › “Show rosters” (on a phone “Rosters”).
matchSetup.q_rosterWays: How can I get a team's roster in?
matchSetup.a_rosterWays: In “Edit roster” on the team's card: 1. type the players in “Add new player”; 2. “Upload PDF” (Local): the team's roster PDF or the Einsatzliste; 3. “Remote”: the coach uploads the PDF on roster.openvolley.app with your upload PIN (or the team sends it from the manager page), and you “Accept” it; 4. “Choose players”: tick who plays from the players the app knows for this team; 5. “Load saved team” (signed in): a team saved in your account; 6. “Add from club” (signed in, your club): from the club's licence lists; 7. in a test match, “Load TEST roster”. In Global mode the rosters come from Excel (“Import rosters”). A restored match brings its rosters with it. A saved team loads its players and bench officials in one tap: check the numbers for this game. The test players of “Load TEST roster” disappear when you load a game from the schedule or type another team name; the players you added yourself stay.
matchSetup.a_choosePlayers: It lists every player the app knows for this team (its saved team and the players of an imported Einsatzliste). Tick who plays this match (“All” ticks everyone), then tap “Use n players”: they go on the roster with their numbers. Add or change numbers in the roster afterwards.
matchSetup.q_numbers: Can I save a roster without shirt numbers?
matchSetup.a_numbers: Yes. Players without a number are kept: their empty # is highlighted and a note says how many still need one. Add the numbers when you know them (an Einsatzliste never has any). The coin toss waits until every player of both teams has a number.

coinToss.q_record: How do I record the coin toss?
coinToss.a_record: Toss the coin with both captains first. Then set the result on this page: “Switch sides” puts each team on its side, “Switch serve” gives the first service to the right team.
coinToss.tip_record: Tap “Switch sides” until each team stands on its side.
coinToss.q_serve: How do I select which team serves first?
coinToss.a_serve: The ball shows the team that serves first. Tap “Switch serve” to give the service to the other team.
coinToss.tip_serve: Tap here to give the first service to the other team.
coinToss.q_sides: How do I choose court sides?
coinToss.a_sides: Team A is shown on the left, Team B on the right. Tap “Switch sides” to swap them.
coinToss.tip_sides: The two teams as they start: Team A left, Team B right.
coinToss.q_start: How do I start the match?
coinToss.a_start: When the sides and the service are done, tap “Confirm coin toss result”. Signatures still missing can follow on the scoring screen. The app checks the connection and opens the scoring screen.
coinToss.tip_start: Tap here to confirm the coin toss and open the scoring screen.
coinToss.a_signatures: The captain and the coach of each team. Tap “Sign A” or “Sign B”, then “Captain” or “Coach”. They sign on the screen, or on their own phone with “Sign on phone”. They can also sign later, during the warm-up: the scoring screen shows a flashing “Missing signature” for their team, and set 1 starts only once all four have signed. An easy match needs no signatures.
coinToss.q_lineups: Where do I enter the starting line-ups?
coinToss.a_lineups: On the scoring screen, before the first rally of each set. Tap “Line-up” on each team's side and enter the six players for positions I to VI. Liberos are not in the starting line-up.
coinToss.q_gameCaptain: What if the team captain is not on court?
coinToss.a_gameCaptain: When the team captain is not among the six, the line-up dialog shows “Game captain” (optional): choose the player who acts as captain. If you leave “None”, the app asks before the set starts. During the set it asks again only when the game captain leaves the court. This follows “Manage captain on court” in the options (on by default).
coinToss.q_mistake: I recorded the coin toss wrong?
coinToss.a_mistake: Before “Confirm coin toss result”, just switch again. After it, the page is locked: change Team A or the first serve in Match › “Corrections”. Before the first rally of set 1, a new Team A there redoes the coin toss (Team A on the left).
coinToss.q_rosterDialog: Can I still change a roster at the coin toss?
coinToss.a_rosterDialog: Yes: “Show roster” under each team opens it. “+ Add player”, delete a player, add or delete a bench official.
coinToss.q_connectionChecks: What are the “Connection checks” after the coin toss?
coinToss.a_connectionChecks: Before the first set the app checks that the server, the backups and the connected tablets answer. A warning lists what does not; “Proceed anyway” starts the match: scoring works offline and the changes are sent later.

scoreboard.q_startRally: How do I start the first rally?
scoreboard.a_startRally: Enter both line-ups first. Tap “Start set” for the first rally of a set, then “Start rally” at each service whistle. In continuous play (in the options, “Point entry”) there is no “Start rally”: after “Start set”, Point A and Point B stay on screen.
scoreboard.a_missingSignature: The coach or the captain of that team has not signed the roster yet. Tap it: the team's roster opens, they check it and sign, on the screen or on their own phone. “Start set” in set 1 waits until the coach and the captain of both teams have signed.
scoreboard.tip_startRally: Tap here at the service whistle. Both line-ups are needed before the first rally.
scoreboard.q_awardPoint: How do I award a point?
scoreboard.a_awardPoint: When the rally ends, tap the point button of the team that won it. The app adds the point, moves the service and rotates the team that wins the service back. In continuous play, hold the button for 2 seconds (it fills up and reads “Hold”): a short tap gives no point.
scoreboard.tip_awardPoint: Tap the team's point button when the rally ends.
scoreboard.q_timeout: How do I call a timeout?
scoreboard.a_timeout: Between rallies, tap the team's “TO” box. Check the dialog and tap “Confirm time-out”: a 30-second countdown starts. “Stop timeout” ends it early. Each team has 2 time-outs per set; for a third, the app opens a warning that records it as an improper request (or a delay if the time-out already started). No time-out during the interval between sets.
scoreboard.tip_timeout: Tap here to call a time-out for this team, between rallies.
scoreboard.q_substitution: How do I make a substitution?
scoreboard.a_substitution: Between rallies, tap the player on court and choose “Substitution”, then the player who comes in. Or drag a bench player onto the court player (long-press on a tablet). Then confirm. Players who may not come in are greyed, with the reason. Or tap the team’s “Substitution” box under the score: who comes in, then who goes out (several pairs at once), then Confirm.
scoreboard.tip_substitution: Tap a player on court to substitute, drag a bench player onto the court, or tap the Substitution box under the score.
scoreboard.q_libero: How does the libero come in?
scoreboard.a_libero: Tap a back-row player (I, V or VI) and choose “Libero”, or drag the libero from the bench onto that player. Not the player who is about to serve. A rally must be played between two libero replacements. A replacement made before the whistle can still be entered after “Start rally”: tap the player, the menu then shows only “Libero”.
scoreboard.tip_libero: Drag the libero from the bench onto a back-row player (I, V, VI).
scoreboard.q_undo: How do I undo an action?
scoreboard.a_undo: Tap “Undo” and confirm. It takes back the last action of the current set: a point, a time-out, a substitution or a sanction. During a rally it takes back the rally start together with the last point. Tap it again to go further back.
scoreboard.tip_undo: Tap “Undo” to take back the last action. Repeat to go further back.
scoreboard.q_sanction: How do I record a sanction?
scoreboard.a_sanction: Tap the player on court and choose “Sanction”: “Warning” (yellow), “Penalty” (red), “Expulsion” (red and yellow together) or “Disqualification” (red and yellow apart). For a bench player or a bench official, tap them in the bench list. Then confirm.
scoreboard.tip_sanction: Tap a player to open their menu, then choose the sanction.
scoreboard.q_lineup: How do I enter the line-up?
scoreboard.a_lineup: Before the first rally of the set, tap “Line-up” on each team's side. Type the number for each position I to VI, or tap or drag a player from “Available players”, then tap “Confirm”. Both teams need all six positions. The first line-up stays covered (“Line-up set”) until the other team's line-up is in.
scoreboard.tip_lineup: Tap “Line-up” on this side to enter the team's six starting players.
scoreboard.a_shortcuts: Switch on “Keyboard shortcuts” in the options. The keys are A and L for a point to the left or right team, Q and P for a time-out, X and N to exchange the liberos, Backspace for undo, Enter to start the rally or confirm, and Escape to cancel. Change them with “Configure keys” in the scoring screen's options. In continuous play, hold A or L for 2 seconds; Enter only starts the set.
scoreboard.q_setEnd: What happens at the end of a set?
scoreboard.a_setEnd: At 25 points with a 2-point lead (15 in the deciding set), the app shows the set end with the score and the winner. Check the end time and tap “Confirm”. If the last point was wrong, tap “Decision change” instead.
scoreboard.tip_setEnd: The set counter shows the sets each team has won.
scoreboard.a_set5: The deciding set (set 5, or set 3 in a best of 3) goes to 15 points with a 2-point lead. Toss the coin again before it: “Switch sides” and “Switch serve” set the sides and the service (the “SERVE” ball beside the buttons shows who serves), then tap “Confirm set 5 setup” (“Confirm set 3 setup” in a best of 3). At 8 points the teams change courts.
scoreboard.tip_set5: The set indicator shows which set is played and the results so far.
scoreboard.q_changeDecision: How do I change a scoring decision?
scoreboard.a_changeDecision: After a point, tap “Decision change”: “Assign to other team” or “Replay the rally”; the dialog shows the new score and who serves. Time-outs, substitutions or a libero replacement recorded after that point are listed under “Taken back first” and undone with it. During a rally, “Replay rally” replays it. To take the game back further in this set, use Match › “Go back”; older mistakes are fixed in Match › Corrections. In continuous play the button is “Decision change / Replay”, with “Assign to other team”, “Replay” and a third option, “Rally replayed”: it records only the replay, and the last point stays. Nothing is chosen until you tap an option. After a replay, “Decision change” offers “Point A” or “Point B”: the referee gives the rally after all, and the point takes the replay’s place (“Undo” brings the replay back).
scoreboard.tip_changeDecision: “Undo” takes back the last action. After a point, “Decision change” is next to it.
scoreboard.q_coveredLineup: Why is one team's court grey with “Line-up set”?
scoreboard.a_coveredLineup: Until both line-ups of the set are entered, the first one stays covered, so the other team cannot see it: its court shows “Line-up set”, and its bench, serve number and last action are hidden. “Show line-up” shows it to you, “Change line-up” edits it. Everything shows once the second line-up is in.

matchEnd.q_reviewResults: How do I review the match results?
matchEnd.a_reviewResults: The results table shows set-by-set scores, timeouts used, substitutions per set, set durations, and total match duration.
matchEnd.tip_reviewResults: This table shows the complete match results and statistics.
matchEnd.q_signatures: How do I collect final signatures?
matchEnd.a_signatures: First the two captains sign under “Team captains”. Then the officials sign in this order: assistant scorer (if any), scorer, 2nd referee (if any), 1st referee. Tap “Tap to sign” in each box.
matchEnd.tip_signatures: Tap a signature field to open the signing pad and collect the signature.
matchEnd.q_exportPdf: How do I export the scoresheet as PDF?
matchEnd.a_exportPdf: Tap “Scoresheet” and choose “Preview”, “Print” or “Save PDF”. It works before and after the approval.
matchEnd.tip_exportPdf: Tap here to view, print or save the scoresheet.
matchEnd.q_downloadJson: How do I download the match data?
matchEnd.a_downloadJson: “Confirm and approve” downloads a ZIP with the match data (JSON) and the PDF. During the match, Match › “Download game data (JSON)” saves this match's backup file, encrypted with the game PIN and the referee PIN. Both can restore the match (“Restore match” on Home).
matchEnd.tip_downloadJson: “Confirm and approve” saves the match data and makes the scoresheet.
matchEnd.q_reopenSet: How do I reopen a set to make corrections?
matchEnd.a_reopenSet: Tap “Reopen last set” to go back to the scoring screen. All signatures are cleared and must be collected again. After the approval, “Reopen match” reopens a test match, or a match whose approval has not reached the server yet. Once the server has closed it, only an admin can reopen it.
matchEnd.tip_reopenSet: Tap here to reopen the last set. All signatures are cleared.
matchEnd.q_signOnPhone: Can someone sign on their own phone?
matchEnd.a_signOnPhone: Yes. Tap the signature box, then “Sign on phone”, and let them scan the code. Keep this window open until the signature arrives, then tap “Use signature”. It needs the internet or the hall network.
matchEnd.q_approveWithPin: Can a referee approve without drawing a signature?
matchEnd.a_approveWithPin: Yes, with an OpenVolley account. Tap “Approve with PIN” under the box: the official types their own approval PIN. For a referee, their account's e-mail must be entered for them in the match setup (“Email (optional)” under the referee). It needs an internet connection and a match saved online.
matchEnd.a_approve: When every signature is in, tap “Confirm and approve”. If the sheet has something odd, the app lists it first: correct it or tap “Approve anyway”. The app downloads a ZIP with the match data and the scoresheet PDF: keep the scoresheet window open until the PDF is ready. The match is then approved and closed on the server.
matchEnd.q_pdfFailed: It says the PDF is not ready: what now?
matchEnd.a_pdfFailed: “Retry” makes the PDF again. “Approve without PDF” approves the match now: then create the PDF with “Create the PDF” before you close the match, so that it reaches the server. “Cancel” leaves the match not approved.
matchEnd.a_closeMatch: After the approval, “Close match” marks the match final on the server and removes it from this device. Save or print the PDF first if you need a copy on this device.
matchEnd.q_finalMail: Who gets the final scoresheet by e-mail?
matchEnd.a_finalMail: Where the league sends final scoresheets, the PDF is mailed a few minutes after the approval to the scorer, the referees (their accounts, or the e-mail typed for them in the match setup) and each team's contact. Type a team's contact in the match setup (“Team contact email (optional)”) or later in Match › “Edit match info” › “Team contacts”.
matchEnd.q_remarksSignature: A referee coach must sign too?
matchEnd.a_remarksSignature: Tap “Add a signature to the remarks”, type the role and the name, then sign. It is printed in the remarks.
matchEnd.a_technicalRemarks: At match end, “Add technical remark” records something for the administration (a device problem, a correction) that is not printed on the scoresheet: it is kept with the match and sent with the final scoresheet, and the signatures stay. “Edit remarks” changes the remarks printed on the sheet.
matchEnd.a_downloadLogs: It saves the app's log of this match as a file, for support when something went wrong.

manualAdjustments.q_editScores: How do I correct a set score?
manualAdjustments.a_editScores: In the “Set results” card, tap “Correct final score”: a point added after the last point, or the last point removed. In “Advanced: event log” any point can be given to the other team or removed; the serve, the rotations and the score after it are recalculated.
manualAdjustments.tip_editScores: Corrections: the score, the set results, the time-outs, the substitutions and the sanctions.
manualAdjustments.q_editTeams: How do I edit team information?
manualAdjustments.a_editTeams: At the match end, open the “Teams” tab to change names, colours, players and bench officials. The “Match info” tab holds the hall, the date, the officials and the team contacts; during the match it opens with Match › “Edit match info”, and there it also holds each team's shirt colour. Then tap “Save changes”.
manualAdjustments.tip_editTeams: Teams: names, colours, players and bench officials.
manualAdjustments.q_editEvents: How do I correct a time-out, a substitution or a sanction?
manualAdjustments.a_editEvents: Use the “Time-outs”, “Substitutions”, “Sanctions”, “Libero” and “Line-up” cards, or “Advanced: event log” for any entry: each row has “Edit” and “Remove”. A preview shows what changes on the scoresheet before you confirm. What follows the entry is recalculated, and an entry that no longer fits is listed under “Check these entries”.
manualAdjustments.tip_editEvents: Add, edit or remove time-outs, substitutions and sanctions here.
manualAdjustments.q_saveChanges: How do I save my changes?
manualAdjustments.a_saveChanges: Corrections are saved one by one when you confirm them. Changes in “Teams” and “Match info” are saved together with “Save changes” at the top. “Close” asks before it drops unsaved changes.
manualAdjustments.tip_saveChanges: Saves the changes in “Teams” and “Match info”.
manualAdjustments.q_whereCorrections: Where do I correct a mistake?
manualAdjustments.a_whereCorrections: During the match: Match › “Corrections” (the correction board on a tablet or a computer, the list on a phone), or Match › “Go back” when the referees take back part of the set. At the match end: the “Corrections” button. The list saves each correction when you confirm it, the board when you tap “Save”. Every correction is a technical remark: listed in Corrections and at the match end, not printed on the scoresheet, sent with the final scoresheet e-mail. A line the rules want on paper goes in the remarks; for any other correction choose “Remark on the scoresheet” to note it there too.
manualAdjustments.q_missedPoint: I forgot a point during the set?
manualAdjustments.a_missedPoint: On the correction board, tap “+” for the team; in the list, “Add a missed point”. It is added at the current score with its rotation and service, as the point button does. If the last point went to the wrong team, tap “Last point went to the wrong team”.
manualAdjustments.q_serveSidesLineup: How do I fix the serve, the sides or the line-up?
manualAdjustments.a_serveSidesLineup: In Corrections: “Change who serves first”, “Switch sides” and “Reopen set”, and the “Coin toss” card. “Fix the line-up” changes a starting line-up, also after rallies were played; “Forward” and “Back” rotate a team that stands one position off. The rotations after it are recalculated.
manualAdjustments.a_signaturesCleared: A correction that changes the scoresheet clears the signatures collected at the match end. Collect them again. An approved match is read-only: reopen it first.
manualAdjustments.q_editRoster: Can I change a roster during the match?
manualAdjustments.a_editRoster: Yes: Match › Edit home roster or Edit away roster. Changes after the coin toss are logged in the corrections and in the remarks. A number changed there, or in Corrections › Player numbers, changes for the whole match: every entry before and after shows the new number.
manualAdjustments.q_goBack: The referees take the game back (wrong server, wrong positions, illegal substitution)?
manualAdjustments.a_goBack: Between rallies, open Match › “Go back”. Choose the score where it went wrong, then what it was, whose points since then are cancelled and who gets the point and the service. Check the score, the serve and the line-ups, then tap “Resume”. The app writes the remark on the scoresheet; cancelled points pass the serve but do not count. It works only in the set being played; for an earlier set, use Corrections and tell the referee.
manualAdjustments.q_editMatchInfo: How do I fix the hall, the date or an official during the match?
manualAdjustments.a_editMatchInfo: Match › “Edit match info”: hall, city, league, game number, match type, date, team contacts and officials, and each team's shirt colour (the team names stay as on the scoresheet). Tap “Save changes”; “Close” goes back to the match.
manualAdjustments.a_board: On a tablet in landscape or a computer, Match › “Corrections” opens the correction board: the scoreboard with every part correctable. “+” and “−” add or remove a point (or tap the score and type it: the difference goes in as the team’s points in a row), the time-out boxes add, move or remove a time-out, a tap on a player substitutes, sanctions or renumbers them, the arrows rotate a team and “Starting line-up” corrects the line-up. The board redraws at once and nothing is saved until you tap “Save”: then every change is written together and listed in the correction log. “Undo” takes back the last change, “Cancel” throws them all away. “List” shows the cards instead (phones always use them), with the event log and “Reopen set”. A point that would end the set is given with the point button.

contextHelp.videoOffline: The video plays when this device is online.
contextHelp.videoUnavailable: This video is not available right now.

sections.teamManager: My teams: squad and game rosters

scoring.q_doubleTap: I tapped twice: why was only one point given?
scoring.a_doubleTap: On “Start rally” and the point buttons, a second tap at the same place within 450 ms of the one before is taken as a double tap and ignored (“Not counted” shows): a double tap or a bouncing finger gives no second point and starts no new rally. A tap aimed at the other button counts as soon as you can see it. The keyboard keys act at once. The options also have “Check accidental rally start” and “Check accidental point award”. In continuous play a point needs a hold, so a double tap gives none.
scoring.q_serveRotation: How do I see who serves and the rotation?
scoring.a_serveRotation: The “SERVE” box in the top corner of the serving team's side shows the number of the server; the ball is next to that player on court. The court shows each team's positions I to VI. The app rotates a team when it wins the service back. A wrong rotation is fixed in Match › Corrections with “Fix the line-up”.
scoring.q_scoreDisplay: What does the score display show?
scoring.a_scoreDisplay: The points of the set, the sets won and the serving team. Each team's side shows its time-outs and substitutions in this set (“Time-out”, “Substitution”): tap them to record one. Match › Show sanctions and results lists every set. For more room, “Hide header” (the arrow under the header) and “Hide toolbar” fold them away; the arrow brings them back.
scoring.q_phone: Can I score on a phone?
scoring.a_phone: Yes. In the options, set “Screen mode” to “Auto” or “Smartphone”, and hold the phone upright. The score, the court, the time-outs, the substitutions and the point buttons fit on one screen. On a tablet, scoring is in landscape: held upright, it asks you to turn it.
scoring.q_matchMenu: What is in the Match menu?
scoring.a_matchMenu: “Match” on the scoring screen (on a phone ☰): “Show rosters”, “Show sanctions and results”, “History” (every rally and action), “Set preview” (the set as it prints), “Open remarks recording”, “Show match setup”, “Corrections”, “Go back”, “Options”, “Pair a phone (keyboard)” (type on your phone into this device's text fields), “Show on a scoreboard” (a TV, tablet or LED board follows the score with a code) and “Stop the match” (default, incomplete team or impossibility, with remarks).
scoring.q_replay: How do I record a replayed rally?
scoring.a_replay: During a rally, “Replay rally” (on a phone “Replay”) replays it without a point. After a point, “Decision change” › “Replay the rally” takes it back; the dialog shows the score before and after each choice.

subsTimeouts.q_subLimit: How many substitutions does a team have?
subsTimeouts.a_subLimit: Six per set. The “SUB” box counts them and turns amber at 5. A starting player can leave once and come back once, only for the player who replaced them. After the sixth, a further request is an improper request.
subsTimeouts.q_injury: A player is injured: what do I do?
subsTimeouts.a_injury: Tap the player on court and choose “Injury”, then a substitute. If no legal substitution is possible, the app offers an exceptional substitution. After an exceptional substitution, that player cannot play again in this match.
subsTimeouts.q_liberoOut: How does the libero leave the court?
subsTimeouts.a_liberoOut: Tap the libero on court and choose “Libero out”: the replaced player comes back. A rally must be finished first (“After finished rally”). When the libero rotates to the front row, the app takes the libero out and shows “Libero OUT”: tap “OK”. Later it asks “Libero IN?” for the back-row player; “Not now” stops this question for that team until the end of the set. “Exchange libero” swaps the two liberos.
subsTimeouts.q_liberoUnable: The libero cannot play any more?
subsTimeouts.a_liberoUnable: Tap the libero and choose “Unable to play”: declared unable, or injury or illness. If the team has no other libero, the app lets you designate another player as the new libero. An injured libero may play again (tap him: “Able to play again”) as long as no new libero was re-designated in his place.
subsTimeouts.q_captainRing: Why is a number circled on the bench?
subsTimeouts.a_captainRing: The circle marks the team captain, as on the paper scoresheet. A libero who is captain has the circle next to the L1 or L2 tag.
subsTimeouts.q_benchRequests: A card says “Time-out request” or “Line-up for set 2”?
subsTimeouts.a_benchRequests: The team's bench tablet sent a request. The cards stand in the top right corner and can be folded. “Grant time-out” opens the time-out dialog, “Substitute” the substitution of that pair, “Review and accept” the line-up dialog filled in by the bench: check it and tap “Confirm”. Granting waits while a rally is in play. “Decline” asks for a reason (optional), which the bench sees. You can also record it by hand as usual: the card closes once it is recorded.
subsTimeouts.q_requestWarning: Why does a warning open when I record a time-out or a substitution?
subsTimeouts.a_requestWarning: The app checks the rules for requests: a third time-out, a seventh substitution, a second substitution request of the same team in one interruption, a player who may not come in, or a request after the team's delay warning. The warning says why and offers what to record, such as “Record as improper request” or a delay sanction. “Continue anyway” records nothing more when the referee allowed it (not offered for a third time-out or a seventh substitution).
subsTimeouts.q_gameCaptain: The team captain went off court: who is game captain?
subsTimeouts.a_gameCaptain: The app asks “Game captain”: tap the player on court who acts as captain (the last game captain is offered first, marked “Last”). Until one is chosen, a “Game captain” button shows on that team's side. The game captain stays until they leave the court, the team captain comes back or the set ends. This needs “Manage captain on court” in the options (on by default).
subsTimeouts.q_subDialog: How does the substitution dialog work?
subsTimeouts.a_subDialog: Tap the team's “Substitution” box (on a phone “SUB”). Tap who comes in, then who goes out: only legal players are shown (a substituted starter only for his substitute, never the libero). The pair goes into the list and the dialog asks for the next one; “Confirm” records them all, “Cancel” none. “Recorded” lists this set's substitutions; at 6 of 6 only “Injury / exceptional” is left. During a rally the box shows only that list.

sanctions.q_teamSanctions: How do I record an improper request or a delay?
sanctions.a_teamSanctions: Under each team's “TO” and “SUB” boxes are “Improper request” and “Delay warning” (on a small screen under “IR & delays”). A team has one improper request: then the button gives way to an “Improper request” box. After the delay warning the button becomes “Delay penalty”: point and service to the opponent. The app writes them on the scoresheet.
sanctions.q_ladder: Why did my delay warning become a penalty?
sanctions.a_ladder: The sanctions follow the rules. A second improper request counts as a delay. A delay after a delay warning is a delay penalty. The dialog tells you before you confirm.
sanctions.q_penaltyPoint: Who gets the point after a penalty?
sanctions.a_penaltyPoint: The opponent gets the point and the service. The app adds them and rotates the team if needed. A delay penalty given before the line-ups are entered is added once both line-ups are in.
sanctions.q_expulsion: What happens after an expulsion or a disqualification?
sanctions.a_expulsion: An expelled player sits out the rest of the set, a disqualified one the rest of the match. A player on court must be replaced: the app asks for the substitution, an exceptional one if no legal one is left (then he cannot play again in this match).
sanctions.a_warningOnce: A team gets one warning per match. After it, “Warning” is greyed out for every member of that team. Further misconduct is a penalty or more.
sanctions.q_fixSanction: I recorded the wrong sanction: how do I fix it?
sanctions.a_fixSanction: If it is the last action, tap “Undo”. Otherwise open Match › Corrections: in the “Sanctions” card, edit or remove it, or tap “Add sanction”. The correction log shows the change to the referee.
sanctions.q_lateRequest: The rally was stopped because of a late request: how do I record it?
sanctions.a_lateRequest: During the rally, tap “Replay rally”: it records only the replay. Then give the delay sanction with that team's “Delay warning” button (or “Delay penalty” if it already has a warning).

setEnd.q_interval: How does the interval between sets work?
setEnd.a_interval: The countdown starts when you confirm the set end. It lasts 3 minutes: change it in the options under “Set 2-3 interval duration”. “End set interval” ends it early. The referee tablet shows the same countdown.
setEnd.q_nextSet: Do I change the sides and the service for the next set?
setEnd.a_nextSet: No. The app changes the sides and gives the first service to the right team by itself. Enter both line-ups, then tap “Start set”.
setEnd.q_courtSwitch: How does the change of courts at 8 points work?
setEnd.a_courtSwitch: When a team reaches 8 points in the deciding set, the app shows “Court switch required”. Let the teams change, then tap “Switch courts”. If a correction takes the score back below 8, the app asks to switch back.
setEnd.q_syncAtSetEnd: The set end says “Offline. Data saved locally.” or “Sync failed”?
setEnd.a_syncAtSetEnd: The set is safe on this device. The message closes by itself and the set goes to the server when the connection is back. If it says “Sync failed”, tap “Proceed anyway” (it also goes on by itself after 5 seconds). In a browser, the app can also download a backup at the set end (“Auto-download data at set end” in the options).
setEnd.q_matchEnd: What happens after the last set?
setEnd.a_matchEnd: The app shows the match end with the result. Confirm the end time: the match end page opens for the signatures and the approval.

connections.q_how: How do I connect the referee and bench tablets?
connections.a_how: Open the menu (☰) in the header and tap “Connect tablets”. Step 1: choose how the tablets connect. Step 2: choose the tablet. Step 3: scan the code with the tablet's camera and enter the PIN shown.
connections.a_whichWay: “Hall Wi-Fi”: the hall has Wi-Fi and this computer is on it. “Wi-Fi from this computer”: no hall Wi-Fi; the desktop app makes its own (Windows, Linux). “Internet”: the tablets have mobile data; you must be signed in. “Bluetooth” is a last resort, on Linux only.
connections.q_desktopNeeded: Why does it say “Needs the desktop app”?
connections.a_desktopNeeded: Tablets on the local network need the OpenVolley desktop app (or a venue box) on this computer: it serves the referee, bench and livescore pages. In a browser, choose “Internet”.
connections.q_pageNotLoading: The tablet joins, but the page does not load?
connections.a_pageNotLoading: Some hall Wi-Fis keep devices apart: choose “Wi-Fi from this computer” or “Internet”. On Windows, let OpenVolley through the firewall: Windows Security › Firewall & network protection › Allow an app through firewall › OpenVolley › tick “Public”.
connections.q_noInternet: The tablet says “No internet” on the laptop's Wi-Fi?
connections.a_noInternet: That is normal: the laptop's Wi-Fi has no internet. Choose “Stay connected”, then scan the code of the tablet's role.
connections.q_pin: Where is the PIN, and why is it refused?
connections.a_pin: Step 3 shows the PIN of the chosen tablet. The links and codes never contain it. A tablet that is off is refused: turn it on in step 2 (“Let … in”). After too many wrong PINs, wait a few minutes.
connections.a_hallServer: The OpenVolley desktop app runs a server for the tablets on the hall network, with no internet needed. A venue box or the downloadable server does the same. With internet, the match also syncs to the cloud.
connections.q_hallNetwork: Which Wi-Fi should the hall server use?
connections.a_hallNetwork: Give the scorer, referee and bench tablets their own Wi-Fi with a password (WPA2 or WPA3) that spectators do not get. On an open or shared Wi-Fi, others in the hall can read the match traffic, including the PINs and the team lists.
connections.a_internetTablets: Only with “Internet”. Then you must be signed in, and the match must be synced (the status says Synced) before the tablets find it. On the hall network, no internet is needed.
connections.q_testMatch: Can I try the tablets with a test match?
connections.a_testMatch: Yes. Start a test match and turn the tablet on in “Connect tablets”; its code opens it directly. A tablet that picks from the list over the internet taps “Switch to test matches”. Test matches never show on the online livescore.
connections.a_connectToServer: Over the internet, choose “Online (automatic)”. On the hall network, choose “Local server” and type the address from “Connect tablets” (step 3, “Type the address”). A scanned code usually skips this screen.
connections.q_status: How do I see which tablets are connected?
connections.a_status: The chip in the scorer's header (for example 2/3) counts the connected tablets; tap it to see which one is missing. Step 2 of “Connect tablets” shows each tablet: connected, waiting for the tablet, or off.

referee.q_open: How do I open the referee tablet?
referee.a_open: Scan the referee code in the scorer's “Connect tablets”, then enter the PIN and tap “Enter”. Without the code: open referee.openvolley.app, choose “Online (automatic)”, tap “Select game”, pick the game, enter the “Connection PIN” and tap “Enter”. On a phone or tablet with OpenVolley, Home › menu › “Referee dashboard” opens it too.
referee.a_noGames: The scorer must have the match open with the referee tablet turned on (“Connect tablets”, step 2). Over the internet, the match must be synced first. Tap “Load games” to look again. A test match is listed after “Switch to test matches”.
referee.q_view: What do 1 REF and 2 REF change?
referee.a_view: They turn the court to match where you stand: 1 REF for the 1st referee on the stand, 2 REF for the 2nd referee on the scorer's side. The score and the data stay the same.
referee.q_shows: What does the referee tablet show?
referee.a_shows: The score and the sets, the serving team, both line-ups with the rotation, the time-outs (TO) and substitutions (SUB), the sanctions of a team once it has one, and the last action. Time-outs and intervals show their countdown. “Scoresheet” and “Rosters” are in the header.
referee.q_recorded: What is the “Recorded by the scorer” popup?
referee.a_recorded: When the scorer records a time-out, a substitution or a sanction, every referee tablet shows it in a popup, with the team, the set and the score. Tap “OK”, or it closes by itself after 10 seconds. What is recorded while it is open is added to it. During a time-out the countdown shows in the popup and moves to the court when it closes.
referee.q_offline: It says “Offline: no connection to the scoresheet”?
referee.a_offline: This tablet has lost its connection (Wi-Fi or server) for a few seconds, so the score may be out of date. It reconnects by itself when the network is back; if not, tap “Refresh” in the menu. A yellow “The scorer's device is not connected” means this tablet is fine but the scorer's device is off, asleep or offline: tell the scorer.
referee.q_screen: How do I keep the screen on?
referee.a_screen: Open the menu and switch on “Keep screen on”. The fullscreen button hides the browser bars.
referee.a_bell: Once the referee tablet is turned on, the scorer's header has a bell. Tapping it shows “Scorer needs attention” on the referee tablet, which vibrates where it can. Tap “Acknowledge”.
referee.a_scoresheet: “Scoresheet” shows the live scoresheet, read only; zoom with − and + or “Fit”, and “Turn” rotates it. Signatures, officials and dates of birth stay on the scorer's device. “Rosters” lists both teams' players and team officials. “Close” goes back.
referee.q_benchRequests: What is “Bench asks for a time-out” at the bottom?
referee.a_benchRequests: A bench asked the scorer for a time-out or prepared a substitution on its tablet. It is a notice only: the coach still asks you as always, and the scorer records it. It goes away when the scorer answers or the bench cancels.
referee.q_upright: It says “Please hold the device upright”?
referee.a_upright: On phones and tablets the referee dashboard works upright. Turn the device; the score and the countdowns keep going. On Android, “Enter fullscreen” keeps it upright however you hold it.
referee.a_awaiting: The match starts on the tablet as soon as the scorer confirms the coin toss.

bench.q_open: How do I open the bench tablet?
bench.a_open: Scan your team's bench code in the scorer's “Connect tablets”, enter the team PIN and tap “Connect”. Without the code: open bench.openvolley.app, choose “Online (automatic)”, pick the game (check the game number) and your team, enter the team PIN and tap “Connect”. A test match is listed after “Switch to test matches”.
bench.q_shows: What does the bench tablet show?
bench.a_shows: The score (your team first), the set and the sets, your time-outs (TO) and substitutions (SUB) used, your sanctions, your team on court with the captain, your bench and liberos, and the buttons to send requests to the scorer.
bench.q_requests: Can the coach ask for a time-out or a substitution from the tablet?
bench.a_requests: Yes. “Time-out” sends a time-out request; “Substitution” › who goes off and who comes on › “Send”. The scorer sees it at once and records it, or declines it with a reason. It is an aid only: the coach still asks the referee as always. The × on a button cancels an open request.
bench.a_invalidPin: Check the team PIN and the game number with the scorer. The scorer must turn your bench on in “Connect tablets” (step 2). After too many wrong PINs from one network, wait a few minutes.
bench.a_outage: It rejoins its match by itself when the server is back, and waits for the scoresheet if needed. You do not need to enter the PIN again.
bench.q_roster: How does the coach send the roster?
bench.a_roster: On roster.openvolley.app: choose the game and the team, enter the upload PIN from the scorer and upload the roster PDF. The scorer accepts it in the match setup. A team manager can also send the roster ahead on manager.openvolley.app (“My Teams”).
bench.a_grey: Each button says when it works, for example “After the coin toss”, “After the line-up”, “The set has started”, “Both time-outs used” or “6 substitutions used”. The match shows on the tablet as soon as the scorer confirms the coin toss.
bench.q_lineup: How does the coach send the starting line-up?
bench.a_lineup: After the coin toss, tap “Line-up”, tap a position and then a player until all six are placed, and tap “Send line-up”. Only the scorer sees it until the set starts. The scorer checks it and confirms it; the button then says “Recorded by the scorer”.
bench.q_status: What do “The scorer has it”, “Granted” and “Declined” mean?
bench.a_status: “Sent – waiting for the scorer”: on its way. “The scorer has it”: the scorer sees it. “Granted” or “Accepted”: recorded. “Declined: …”: the scorer said no, with the reason. “Not sent – no connection”: try again when the tablet is online.
bench.q_scorerAway: It says “The scorer's device is not connected”?
bench.a_scorerAway: The scorer's laptop or tablet is off, asleep or has lost its connection, so the score may be out of date and your requests wait. Tell the scorer; the notice goes once the scorer's device is back.

livescore.q_open: How do I follow a match live?
livescore.a_open: Open livescore.openvolley.app and choose the game. No PIN is needed. Or scan the livescore code in the scorer's “Connect tablets”.
livescore.a_shows: The team names, the score, the sets and the serving team. It shows no player data.
livescore.a_notListed: The scorer must be online and signed in, with the match started and synced. Test matches never appear on the online livescore. On the hall network, open the livescore address shown in “Connect tablets”.
livescore.q_bigScreen: Can I show the score on a big screen?
livescore.a_bigScreen: Yes. Open the livescore on the screen's computer and choose the game: it fills the page. The browser's fullscreen (F11 on most computers) hides the bars.
livescore.q_stale: It says “Connection problem: showing the last known scores”?
livescore.a_stale: The livescore lost its connection and shows the last score it received. It updates again when the connection is back.
livescore.q_ledBoard: Can the hall's LED scoreboard show the score?
livescore.a_ledBoard: Yes. An LED scoreboard in the hall can follow the match, on the hall network or over the hall's internet. It receives only the team names, the score and the set results, never player names.

handover.q_continueOther: How do I continue a match on another device?
handover.a_continueOther: On the new device, tap “Restore match” on Home. Under “Restore from cloud backup”, enter the game number (“Match #”) and the game PIN, then tap “Search cloud backups”. Choose the newest entry, check the “Restore preview” and tap “Confirm restore”. The new device scores from then on. Nothing found? The cloud copy is at most a minute behind: wait a moment and search again.
handover.q_gamePin: Where do I find the game PIN?
handover.a_gamePin: On Home under “Game PIN”, on the match info page of the match setup (“Send PIN by email” sends it to you), and in the scoring screen under Match › Show PINs.
handover.q_oldDevice: What happens on the old device?
handover.a_oldDevice: It shows “Scored on another device” and stops scoring. The match opens read-only there; its scoresheet can still be viewed. Changes it had not sent are set aside, never sent over the new score. If the other device has closed the match meanwhile, it says so and offers “Load the final result”.
handover.q_takeBack: How do I take scoring back?
handover.a_takeBack: On the old device, tap “Take back scoring here”. It needs a connection. The app first shows the score on the server: compare it with the scoreboard, then tap “Yes, take back scoring here”. The other device is told and stops. If this device has points the server never got, it says so: “Keep this device's score” sends this device's score instead.
handover.a_backups: Match setup › “Backups” shows where this match is saved. The desktop and Android apps save a backup file at every point and action (desktop: Options › Backup › “Open backup folder”; Android: “Export to Documents” copies them out). In Chrome or Edge, pick a backup folder once; other browsers download a file at set end and match end. The desktop app also copies every backup to each USB stick plugged in. Backup files of an official match are encrypted with its game PIN and referee PIN. Signed in, the app also keeps a cloud backup during the match.
handover.q_restoreFile: How do I restore from a backup file?
handover.a_restoreFile: On Home: “Restore match”. Backups the app finds on this device or a USB stick are listed under “Saved on this device or a drive”: tap “Restore”. Another file: “Restore from local file” › “Select backup file”. Check the “Restore preview” and tap “Confirm restore”. A backup of an official match is encrypted: type its game PIN or referee PIN when asked. Test matches open without a PIN.
handover.q_restoreRefused: Why can't I restore this backup?
handover.a_restoreRefused: The match is closed on the server, so a backup of it cannot be restored. Load the official version with the game number and the game PIN instead.
handover.q_lostPins: Nobody has the PINs of a backup file any more?
handover.a_lostPins: The league can open backup files with its recovery key, which it keeps offline. Contact support.

syncOffline.a_offlineScoring: Yes. Everything is saved on this device first, and scoring works fully offline. The changes go to the server when the connection is back.
syncOffline.q_switch: What does the Online switch do?
syncOffline.a_switch: It is in the header. “Offline” stops every connection to the cloud: nothing is synced until you switch back to “Online”. Scoring is not affected.
syncOffline.q_status: What does the sync status mean?
syncOffline.a_status: “Connected”: all is synced. “Syncing...”: changes are going up. “Ready”: connected, nothing to sync (Home, or a test match). “Offline (n waiting)”: no connection, n changes are waiting. “Local only”: the tablets run on the hall network while the cloud is out of reach. “Sign in to sync”: sign in first. “Update needed”: update the app after this match; the changes wait on this device. “Error”: tap it to see why, then “Retry all”.
syncOffline.a_unsent: Some changes of this match are not on the server yet. They go up as soon as the device is online and signed in. Do not delete this copy before they are sent.
syncOffline.q_signIn: It says “Not signed in: this match is saved on this device only”?
syncOffline.a_signIn: Scoring keeps working. Sign in to save the match to the cloud (referee, livescore, backup); the waiting changes are sent right after.
syncOffline.q_closedServer: What does “Closed on the server” mean?
syncOffline.a_closedServer: The match is approved or closed on the server. This copy can no longer be scored or synced. Open it read-only, load the official version, or remove it from this device. Only an admin can reopen the match.
syncOffline.a_movedDevice: Another device has taken the match over and scores it now. This copy opens read-only. Tap “Take back scoring here” only if you score on this device again.
syncOffline.q_refused: It says “Not synced” with a reason?
syncOffline.a_refused: The server refused this match, for example: the game is already scored by another account, your account waits for approval, or it is not a home game of your club. The match stays safe on this device. The notice tells you what to do.
syncOffline.q_testMatch: Does a test match go online?
syncOffline.a_testMatch: A test match is never saved to the cloud: no cloud backup, no online livescore. Its score does reach referee and bench tablets over the internet: on the tablet, tap “Switch to test matches”.
syncOffline.q_onlineSwitch: Why is the Online switch grey?
syncOffline.a_onlineSwitch: “Online” is on, but nothing answers: no network, or the server cannot be reached. The changes wait on this device (the status beside it says “Offline (n waiting)”) and are sent once the connection is back; the switch turns green again by itself. Switched off, it is offline mode: the app does not try at all.

installUpdates.a_appOrBrowser: app.openvolley.app works in a browser and keeps working offline once it has loaded. The desktop app (Windows, macOS, Linux) adds the tablet server for the hall and saves a backup file at every event. The Android app also saves every event.
installUpdates.q_download: Where do I get the apps?
installUpdates.a_download: On get.openvolley.app (on Home: “Download OpenVolley”): the desktop app for Windows, macOS and Linux, and the Android app (with F-Droid or as an APK). Under the Windows and macOS buttons it shows the file's SHA-256, to check the download.
installUpdates.a_windows: SmartScreen shows this for a new download. Tap “More info”, then “Run anyway”. The installer asks once for an administrator, so the tablets can get through the firewall.
installUpdates.q_macos: macOS does not open the app?
installUpdates.a_macos: The app is signed and notarized by Apple, so macOS opens it like any other app. If macOS still blocks it, it is an older copy: install the current version from get.openvolley.app, drag it to Applications and start it from there.
installUpdates.q_android: How do I install and update the Android app?
installUpdates.a_android: Add the OpenVolley repository in F-Droid (see get.openvolley.app): F-Droid then installs the updates. An APK installed without F-Droid does not update itself, but the app can tell you about new versions.
installUpdates.q_desktopUpdates: How does the desktop app update?
installUpdates.a_desktopUpdates: It downloads updates in the background and installs them when you quit, never during a match. “Restart and update” installs one now. Installed with Flatpak, Snap or another package manager, the updates come from there.
installUpdates.a_webUpdate: Between matches the browser shows “Update available!”: tap “Refresh to update”, or “Later” to keep the current version for now. During a match it never asks, unless an update is needed.
installUpdates.a_updateNeeded: This version is too old for the server. Your changes stay on this device and are sent after the update. In a browser, refresh after this rally; in the app, install the update after this match.

global.a_what: For any tournament or friendly outside the Swiss leagues. There is no sign-in and no game list: games and rosters come from Excel. Teams and players stay on this device.
global.q_switch: How do I switch between Swiss and Global?
global.a_switch: You choose the first time the app opens; later in “Options” › “Tool”. You can only switch while no match is on the device, so delete it first.
global.q_match: How do I start a match?
global.a_match: Tap “Match” on Home. Match setup opens empty: import the game and the rosters, or type them, then tap “Create match”.
global.q_importGames: How do I load a game from Excel?
global.a_importGames: In Match setup, tap “Import games (Excel)” and choose an Excel or CSV file with one row per game (game, date, time, hall, city, league, home, away, best of, referees). Then tap the game. “Template” downloads a ready-made file.
global.q_importRosters: How do I load the rosters?
global.a_importRosters: Tap “Import rosters (Excel)”. The file has one row per person: team, number, first name, last name, role, date of birth. Each team in the file is listed: tap “Home team” or “Away team” beside it.
global.a_stored: No. It is read on this device and nothing of it is stored online.
global.a_rules: Yes. In the match info, set “Points per set” to 25, 21 or 15, and “Deciding set” to 15, 11 or 10.
global.a_nextToName: What the scoresheet shows beside each name: “Use birthdates”, “Use an ID number” or “Use text” (for example a school class).
global.a_backupCode: Match setup › “Backups” › “Cloud” shows a code and the referee PIN. The match's backup and its finished scoresheet are kept online under that code, encrypted with the referee PIN, without an account. Keep both: together they restore the match.
global.q_restore: How do I continue a Global match on another device?
global.a_restore: Home › “Restore match”. Enter the backup code under “Restore from the online backup” and tap “Find backup”; the app then asks for the referee PIN.
global.q_language: Why is there no Swiss German?
global.a_language: Global is for any country, so its language menu has no Swiss German. A device set to Swiss German uses German in Global.
global.tip_match: “Match” starts a full match of the Global tool.

clubManager.q_where: Where do I manage my club?
clubManager.a_where: On manager.openvolley.app, with the same account as in the app. Tap “My Club”. Under it are Requests, Members, Teams, Licences, Invite Codes and API.
clubManager.a_noTab: Your account is not a club manager yet. An admin adds you on the club's page, or sends you a club manager link by e-mail. Ask your club or support@openvolley.app.
clubManager.q_contact: What is the contact e-mail on the club page?
clubManager.a_contact: It gets the final scoresheets of your club's games, for your coaches. Change it and tap “Save”.
clubManager.a_members: Everyone linked to your club: its scorers, its club managers, and new accounts that chose your club. “Remove from club” takes away only the club: they can no longer score your games, and their account stays.
clubManager.q_inviteCodes: How do I give a scorer access?
clubManager.a_inviteCodes: Open “Invite Codes” and tap “New invite code”. Choose Scorer or Referee, how many people may use it (1 to 50) and until when (at most 90 days ahead). Send the code: whoever enters it gets the role and your club at once.
clubManager.q_otherManagers: Can we have more than one club manager?
clubManager.a_otherManagers: Yes. An admin adds them on the club's page, picked from your club's accounts or with a club manager link sent by e-mail. The link works once, for 14 days.
clubManager.a_bell: New sign-ups for your club, and people a team manager proposed. Tap a notice to open your club's Requests.
clubManager.q_myTeams: Can I edit my club's teams myself?
clubManager.a_myTeams: Yes. “My Teams” has every team of your club. Pick the gender and the team, then edit the squad and send game rosters, as a team manager does.
clubManager.q_missingTeam: A team of my club is missing.
clubManager.a_missingTeam: The club's teams are the team names of the official schedule; an admin adds them in the Clubs tab. Write to support@openvolley.app.

teamLinks.a_what: A link for a team's coach or manager. Whoever opens it and signs in becomes team manager of that team: they keep its players up to date and send each game's roster ahead.
teamLinks.a_create: My Club › Teams, then “Create link” at the team. A ready message with the link appears: tap “Share”, “Copy message” or “Copy link”.
teamLinks.q_once: I closed the window. Where is the link?
teamLinks.a_once: It is shown only once. Make a new one with “Create link”.
teamLinks.q_limits: How long does a link work?
teamLinks.a_limits: For 3 people and 30 days; the message says until when. An unused link shows as an open link at the team. “Invite Codes” lists it too, and “Revoke” ends it.
teamLinks.q_who: How do I see who manages a team?
teamLinks.a_who: Their name appears at the team once they opened the link and said yes. The × beside the name takes the team away from them; their account stays.
teamLinks.q_open: I got a team link. What do I do?
teamLinks.a_open: Open it and sign in, or create an account first. When asked whether to manage the team with your e-mail, tap “Yes, with this account”. The team opens under “My Teams”. You don't need to tick anything under “What do you do?”.
teamLinks.q_otherAccount: The link asks about the wrong account.
teamLinks.a_otherAccount: Tap “Use another account” and sign in with the right one. “Forget this link” drops the link from this device.

requests.a_what: At sign-up a person can tick what they do: scorer of a club, referee, team manager or coach of a team, club manager. Each part waits under Requests until someone approves it.
requests.a_where: Club managers: My Club › Requests, or tap the bell. Team managers: at the top of their team in My Teams. Admins: Accounts › Pending.
requests.a_approve: “Approve” gives exactly that part: the role with the club, or the team. “Reject” drops only that part; the account stays. The person's other parts stay for the others to decide.
requests.q_propose: Why does a team manager see “Propose” instead of “Approve”?
requests.a_propose: A team manager's yes is only a proposal. The person shows as proposed, waiting for a club manager, until a club manager or an admin approves. The club's list says who proposed them.
requests.q_emailFirst: Approve says to confirm the e-mail first.
requests.a_emailFirst: The person has not confirmed their e-mail address yet. Ask them to open the link in the mail from OpenVolley, then approve again.
requests.q_waiting: I asked for a role at sign-up. What now?
requests.a_waiting: The manager page lists your requests. An admin or your club approves them, and the page updates by itself. Until then you can score test matches, or enter an invite code if you have one.

teamManager.q_squad: What is the squad of the season?
teamManager.a_squad: Everyone who may play this season, with number and licence. Add them with “Add player”, “Import Einsatzliste” (the PDF from Swiss Volley) or “Add from club”, then tap “Save roster”. Scorers can load this squad in Match setup.
teamManager.a_games: Every game of your team from today on, home and away, from the schedule.
teamManager.q_prepare: How do I send a game's roster?
teamManager.a_prepare: Tap “Prepare roster” at the game. Its page shows when, where, the league and the referees. Untick who does not play, check the numbers, mark C (captain) and L (libero), and tick the officials. Then tap “Send roster”.
teamManager.q_rules: How many players can I send?
teamManager.a_rules: At most 14, and 13 or 14 only with two liberos; at most 2 liberos. One captain, and each number and each official role only once. Fewer than 6 players besides the liberos is only a warning.
teamManager.q_einsatzliste: Can I use the game's Einsatzliste?
teamManager.a_einsatzliste: Yes. On the game page, tap “Import Einsatzliste” and pick the PDF. The players on it are ticked, with your squad's numbers. Check, then send.
teamManager.q_signatures: Do the coach and the captain have to sign here?
teamManager.a_signatures: No, it is optional. They can tap “Sign” now; otherwise they sign in the hall at the coin toss. If you change the roster after signing, sign again or send it without signatures.
teamManager.q_status: What do “Not sent”, “Sent” and “Accepted by the scorer” mean?
teamManager.a_status: “Not sent”: no roster for this game yet. “Sent”: the scorer's tablet gets it as soon as it is online; “Signed” shows when both signed. “Accepted by the scorer”: taken over in the hall; the sent roster is then deleted here, and you can send a new one.
teamManager.q_change: Can I change a roster I sent?
teamManager.a_change: Yes, at any time: “Edit roster”, change it, then “Send roster” again. “Delete roster” takes it back. Send it by the evening before, so the tablet surely has it.
teamManager.a_hall: In Match setup, inside your team's card: “Roster sent by …” with “Accept”, “Show” and “Not now”. “Accept” loads it, and the scorer checks it with the coach.
teamManager.q_privacy: How long is a sent roster kept?
teamManager.a_privacy: Until the scorer accepts it, and at most 14 days after the game.

clubLicences.a_what: The players, scorers and coaches lists from Swiss Volley's club administration. With them, “Add from club” offers your club's people, and green shields mark people who are in the lists.
clubLicences.a_upload: My Club › Licences. Pick the list (Players, Scorers or Coaches), tap “Choose Excel file” and pick the .xlsx export. Check the preview and tap “Save list”. Each upload replaces that list.
clubLicences.a_kept: The file is read on your device. Only licence number, last name, first name and gender are sent and kept; the Excel file is not uploaded.
clubLicences.q_shields: What do the green and gray shields mean?
clubLicences.a_shields: Green: the person is in the club's lists (same licence number, or, without one, the same name when only one person of the club has it). Gray: typed by hand. Tap a gray shield to link the person to someone of the club.
clubLicences.a_addFromClub: It lists the club's players of the team's gender, to add or tick. For an official, search the club's lists by name.
clubLicences.q_gender: Why does it warn about a player's gender?
clubLicences.a_gender: The club's list has that person with the other gender for this game. Check it before the coin toss. A game roster with a player of the wrong gender is refused.
clubLicences.a_delete: Yes, with “Delete list”. Its people are deleted on the server, and scoring tablets drop them the next time they are online.

clubApi.q_what: What is the API page for?
clubApi.a_what: For your club's own website or software: it can read your club's games and live scores, and send rosters. A token acts for your club only. Live scores on a website need no token: use the public widget.
clubApi.q_create: How do I make a token?
clubApi.a_create: Tap “New API token”. Give it a label, tick what it may do, limit it to one team if you want, and set how many days it works (1 to 730; empty means no end).
clubApi.a_scopes: Read: the club, teams, games and matches, without names. Write, if ticked: the roster of a game, a team's squad, the licence lists. A token that can write needs your password.
clubApi.q_once: Where do I see the token again?
clubApi.a_once: Nowhere. It is shown only once, so copy it then; make a new one if it is lost.
clubApi.q_revoke: How do I stop a token?
clubApi.a_revoke: Tap “Revoke”. Software that uses it stops at once, and this cannot be undone.

managerAccounts.q_oneAccount: Do I need a separate account for the manager?
managerAccounts.a_oneAccount: No, it is the same account as in the scorer app. New accounts are made on manager.openvolley.app with “Create account”.
managerAccounts.q_whoSees: Why do I see other pages than my colleague?
